steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour 3 - 9 inch round pans. Sift together the flour, baking soda and salt. Set aside. In a small saucepan, heat water and 4 ounces chocolate until melted. Remove from heat and allow to cool.

In a large bowl, cream 1 cup butter and 2 cups sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in 4 egg yolks one at a time. Blend in the melted chocolate mixture and vanilla. Beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk, mixing just until incorporated.
In a large glass or metal mixing bowl, beat egg whites until stiff peaks form. Fold 1/3 of the whites into the batter, then quickly fold in remaining whites until no streaks remain.

Pour into 3 - 9 inch pans Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean. Allow to cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto wire rack.

To make the Filling: In a saucepan combine 1 cup sugar, evaporated milk, 1/2 cup butter, and 3 egg yolks. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in coconut, pecans and vanilla. Cool until thick enough to spread.
Spread filling between layers and on top of cake. In a small saucepan, melt shortening and 1 ounce of chocolate. Stir until smooth and drizzle down the sides of the cake.

review.reviewBody: This cake is the best! I read a lot of reviews and here is the advice I followed: Do Not Over Mix the batter or it will fall apart! Check cake 20 min. into baking, didn't take the 30 min. the recipe called for. Make 1 1/2 amount of frosting. Add more cornstarch to thicken up frosting or add instant Vanilla pudding. I didn't add pudding, because I wasn't sure WHEN to add it in. Frosting took approx. 30 min. to cook and longer to cool. Plan on investing a good amount of time into it. (But it is well worth it!) Toast the coconut and pecans. Something new I discovered while making this: I must have over mixed because I had trouble getting the cake out of the pan. The bottom layer began to crumble. I stuck the other two pans in the freezer for approx. 1 hr? To remove the frozen cake I placed a towel soaked in very hot water on the pan and it came right out! The cake is easy to handle while frozen and thawed out in the time it took to me to frost it. (I took a good amount of time frosting it) Freezing it didn't dry it out. It tasted and looked amazing! Hope this helps!

This is definitely time consuming, but SO worth the effort. It has become an eight year family tradition and we plan to continue. This is the first time that I can recall getting the filling truly thickened (1 hour cooking on low, wondering if a slightly higher temp and bringing it to a low boil would speed up the process. A double boiler might be necessary for that though.) I also add an extra step of toasting both the pecans and coconut. I prefer to double (or triple) the chocolate at the end. Here’s my photo before adding the chocolate ganache.

This came out amazing!! I had cultured buttermilk powder that called to mix with water so I left the extra water the recipe called for out totally on accident and it still turned out great! I halved the recipe to make a single layer cake in a 7x11 dish. Added a tsp of cornstarch to the frosting before it got to how on the stove as another review said to help to frosting thicken. I make a German chocolate cake every year for my dad's birthday and this recipe was a huge hit! The cake was moist and the coconut-pecan filling was excellent - the best we've ever tasted. Based on the reviews (and family preferences) here are the adaptations I made. 1) I lightly toasted the coconuts and pecans; 2) I used the coconut-pecan frosting to fill between layers and on the top of the cake but made a chocolate ganache frosting for the sides and some decorating; 3) I couldn't find German sweet chocolate, so I used semi-sweet and the cake tasted fine. If I were going to frost the whole cake with the coconut-pecan filling, I would have doubled the batch. I will definitely make this cake again!

I made this for a diabetic with changes and it is sooo good! Instead of white flour I used whole wheat flour. Instead of buttermilk I used unsweetened almond milk with 1 tsp cider vinegar. I also added 1 pkg sugar free butterscotch pudding. Instead of semi sweet chocolate I used 1/4 cup cocoa in 1/2 cup water with 2 tsp of stevia and 1/2 tbls butter and microwaved for 30 seconds. Instead of evaporated milk I used unsweetened almond milk with 2 tblsp of flour. I was out of corn starch. It made 3 one layer cakes. I think at about 15 gms carbohydrates per piece. I froze one for later. I agree it only took me 15 minutes to cook the cake.

Love this recipe! Ck the cake and do not over bake! I made a batch and a half of the frosting. I prefer frosting the whole cake. I wasn't crazy about the chocolate "drippings." It was too thick. I would rather make a small batch of chocolate ganache. I'll do that next time. Maybe poke holes in the cake and run it down the cake itself before putting on the coconut frosting. It turned out beautiful.

I found leaving the top bare left for better presentation. If I had put filling on top, i would have had to double the amount of filling the recipe calls for. Instead I made 5 times the amount of chocolate drizzle and coated the top and let it drizzle down the side. I toasted some coconut and mixed it with a little raw for the edges.

My husband loves this cake he says it is the best German Chocolate he has ever had. I made a double batch of frosting so I could coat the whole cake in it. One batch will only frost the top and give you enough for the middle. The frosting is very hard to get to stick if you don't let it cool long enough so here is my trick. I make the frosting the night before and put it in the fridge. The day I am going to make the cake I set the frosting out on the counter in the morning to get to room temp. This process allows the frosting to set up and not be too hard to spread on the cake when you are ready, it comes out perfect.
I followed the recipe exactly except I made 1 and a half times the amount of filling. Make sure you don't over mix the batter! It'll cause the cake to crumble.

Loved this delicious and moist cake! First time frosting didn't work and was not fixable. Remade frosting with these changes: 1. Used 3 whole eggs instead of just yolks, 2. Used whole-milk evaporated milk instead of 2% (I used 2% the first time), 3. Made sure egg, milk, & sugar mixture came to a boil for 1-3 mins before continuing with recipe. Awesome! Chocolate drizzle around edge makes this special.

Amazing recipe! The best German Chocolate cake i have ever eaten. I followed along with the video and enjoyed baking the cake. I did use 1 1/2 times the recipe for the filling and used 2 tbsp of vanilla pudding which helped it to thicken. I will definitely make it again!!
Make it every year for my former boss. Love it!
My sister has asked me to make this for her as her BIRTHDAY GIFT every year for probably 20 years. It’s labor-intensive but it’s the most like what we remember back when we were kids. Delish!!
Moist and incredible. Swapping to sheet for outdoor cookout.

My husband loves German chocolate cake, so I make it for his birthday each year. I've tried quite a few recipes over the years. I love the flavor and texture on this one. It was a hit at his birthday lunch. I didn't have cake flour, so I just used all-purpose flour. I also used an additional thickener as recommended by other reviewers. However, I didn't have any cornstarch, so I just used two tablespoons of all-purpose flour instead of one tablespoon of cornstarch (following online recommendations). Everything turned out fantastic! This will be my new go-to recipe. If I have cake flour on hand in the future, I will definitely try using it as indicated in the original recipe.
Yes, use chocolate ganache!

I followed most of the tips left by the previous reviewers, particularly ensuring I toasted the pecans and coconut, and refrigerating the cake layers overnight. It's now a standard birthday cake. I converted the measurements to the U.K standard but once done, it was a simple to follow recipe. Thank you.
Delicious. Definitely worth the effort

I wish this recipe would seperate the ingredients into categories like : these ingredients go into making the filling, these ingredients go into making the frosting, and these go into making the actual cake. That way i would know which ingredients to double per the reviews!
It's still a bit of a pain, but worth the effort.
